findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are hardcoded in plain text in the Lambda function's environment variables, committed to source control. Anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration or read access to the repository can retrieve these long-lived static credentials.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so the environment variables (which contain secrets) are protected only by the default service-owned key, and any principal with describe permissions on the function can read the decrypted values. A customer-managed CMK with a restrictive key policy should be used.
The function uses runtime nodejs12.x, which is end-of-life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the execution environment.
No code_signing_config_arn is configured, so the deployment package is not signature-validated before execution and tampering with the artefact between build and deployment would go undetected.

findings.issue_category: missing permissions boundary and trust conditions
findings.description: The Lambda execution role has no permissions_boundary and its trust policy allows lambda.amazonaws.com to assume it with no aws:SourceAccount or aws:SourceArn condition, providing no guardrail against privilege escalation or cross-account confused-deputy use of the role.
